pageProps.review: A guide to resolving the 'User namespaces are not usable by BitBake, possibly due to AppArmor' error on Ubuntu 24.04 Noble Numbat by disabling the AppArmor unprivileged user namespace restriction.
pageProps.description: How to fix the 'User namespaces are not usable' error caused by AppArmor restrictions on Ubuntu 24.04
pageProps.content:
## Fixing AppArmor Unprivileged User Namespace Restriction on Ubuntu 24.04
<mark>AppArmor</mark> is a Linux kernel security module (LSM) that restricts the resources a process can access based on per-program profiles.  
`Ubuntu 24.04 Noble Numbat` onwards, AppArmor has tightened its policy to block <mark>unprivileged user namespaces</mark> by default.  

Yocto/BitBake internally uses <mark>pseudo</mark> (a fakeroot replacement) and user namespaces for build isolation.  
This error commonly occurs when adding layers such as `meta-security` or `meta-virtualization`, or when building container-related recipes.  

The following error occurs when running BitBake.
```doc
{
    "title": "Error: User namespaces are not usable",
    "ref": "https://discourse.ubuntu.com/t/ubuntu-24-04-lts-noble-numbat-release-notes/39890#unprivileged-user-namespace-restrictions"
}
---
ERROR: User namespaces are not usable by BitBake, possibly due to AppArmor.
See https://discourse.ubuntu.com/t/ubuntu-24-04-lts-noble-numbat-release-notes/39890 for more information.
```
```adcard
```
### Apply Immediately (current session)
Use this when immediate application is needed; note that the setting resets on reboot.
```sh
{
    "title": "Disable AppArmor user namespace restriction (temporary)"
}
---
$ sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0
```
### Persist Across Reboots
Apply permanently to persist the setting across reboots.
```sh
{
    "title": "Persist the setting across reboots"
}
---
$ echo 'kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0' | sudo tee /etc/sysctl.d/60-apparmor-namespace.conf
$ sudo sysctl --system
```
